Reviewed only the fix diff from round 1 (2744c4b..dafef60).

The round 1 fixes hold together. Each reply now picks its route (thread, issue-comment or file-only) from whether a review is on GitHub. The only finding is a loose assertion in the new --help test. This repository has no scheduled commands or queued jobs, so nothing can overlap with the changed paths.

comments.body:
**R2-1** · nit · low · confirmed

**The --help test says it checks the header's last line but matches a line four lines earlier**

The case is named "usage: --help prints the writes section to its last line", but it looks for `update <n> <title|-> <file> [<copy>]`. In scripts/redline-gh.sh that text is on line 42. The header runs on to line 46 (the `$REDLINE_BACKUP_DIR` and `<copy>` continuation lines), and line 47 is the blank line where `sed -n '2,/^$/p'` stops. If a later edit put a blank line inside the `update` entry, or a numeric range came back that stopped between lines 42 and 46, `--help` would drop the end of the header and this case would still pass. R1-2 was exactly that kind of truncation.

Proposed fix: Match the header's actual last line, e.g. `has "usage: --help prints the writes section to its last line" "$(cat "$WORK/err")" "unless it already exists (a re-run keeps the first, older body)"`, or compare the last line of the stderr output (`tail -1`) with that text.
